findings.trigger: admins.json exists but cannot be read (invalid JSON after a hand edit or partial copy, or a PermissionError because the file was created/chowned as root while the directory stays writable). get_admin_data() catches the error at :266-269 (or :270-273), logs it and returns the SAME empty document it returns for a missing file: {'discord_admin_users': [], 'admin_notes': {}, 'admin_containers': {}}. add_admin_user() (:293-303) builds on that answer: current = [] + the new id, notes = {}, and passes admin_containers=None, so _save_admin_data_unlocked() asks _load_admin_containers(), which on the same unreadable file also returns {} (:83-86). mkstemp + os.replace need only a writable directory, so the write succeeds -> admins.json now holds exactly one admin, no notes, no container assignments; every previous admin and every B2 scope is gone, and the method returns True ('done'). Any caller of save_admin_data(users, notes) that first read the list through get_admin_data() (e.g. an admin editor showing an empty list) wipes the same way. The auto-action service in this very section treats the identical situation as a defect and refuses to write (ConfigUnreadable, :661-667 'nothing may WRITE on top of a configuration it could not read'); the admin service still does the old thing.
findings.suggestion: Let get_admin_data()/_load_admin_containers() distinguish 'file missing' (empty document is right) from 'file present but unreadable' (raise, e.g. an AdminsUnreadable RuntimeError, as auto_action_config_service does), and make add_admin_user()/save_admin_data() return False with an 'admins.json could not be read; not overwriting it' error in that case instead of replacing the document.
findings.unsure_why: Whether the Discord /addadmin path can reach add_admin_user() with an unreadable file depends on its gate (is_unscoped_admin -> is_user_admin returns False for an unreadable file, which would block it); the panel's admin editor and any other caller of save_admin_data() are outside this section, so I cannot tell which writer reaches the overwrite in practice. The mechanism itself (unreadable == empty, then written back) is certain.

findings.trigger: get_admin_containers() first calls is_user_admin() (:97), which via get_admin_users() reloads the user list and sets _cache_timestamp = now whenever the 5-minute TTL has expired. Only THEN (:101) does it decide whether to reload the container assignment - with the condition 'force_refresh or cache is None or not _is_cache_valid()', and _is_cache_valid() has just been made True by the call one line earlier. So the container assignment is reloaded only when the cache is None (after clear_cache()/an in-process save) or force_refresh=True; the TTL never applies to it. State: an operator narrows an admin's 'admin_containers' in admins.json from outside the process (host edit, docker exec, a second process) -> the user list follows within 5 minutes as designed, the assignment never does until restart -> may_control() keeps answering with the old, wider scope, i.e. the admin keeps controlling containers that were taken away.
findings.suggestion: Evaluate the staleness of the container cache before or independently of the users refresh - e.g. keep an own timestamp for _admin_containers_cache, or reload both caches together inside get_admin_users() when the TTL expires.

findings.trigger: add_admin_user() returns False in two unrelated cases: 'user is already an admin' (:296-297) and 'the save failed' (:302, _save_admin_data_unlocked returned False because the config was unavailable, the directory was unwritable, etc.). A caller cannot tell them apart. State: config dir not writable -> /addadmin for a NEW user -> False -> whichever of the two messages the caller shows, one of them is wrong: either the user is told 'already an admin' for someone who is not, or the duplicate case is told 'failed'. Additionally, when admins.json holds ids as integers (a hand edit; _load_admin_users accepts ints at :161) the duplicate check 'user_id in current' compares str to int and appends a duplicate.
findings.suggestion: Return a three-valued result (added / already_present / failed) or raise on save failure; compare ids as strings (str(x) for x in current) in the duplicate check.
findings.unsure_why: The caller that maps the boolean to a user message is outside this section; the ambiguity in the return value itself is certain.

findings.trigger: admins.json whose top level is not an object (e.g. '[]' or a string after a hand edit), or with 'discord_admin_users': null. _load_admin_users() does admin_data.get(...) -> AttributeError (or 'for user_id in None' -> TypeError); neither the inner except (:169-175) nor the outer (:176) lists these types, so the exception escapes get_admin_users() and is_user_admin(). The same shape escapes _load_admin_containers() (:71, except list at :82-84 has no AttributeError). Every admin check in the bot then raises instead of answering False - every button press that consults the admin list fails with a stack trace rather than a refusal, until the file is fixed. get_admin_data() (:266) DOES catch AttributeError, so the three readers of the same file disagree on the same broken input.
findings.suggestion: Validate 'json.loads(...) is a dict' and 'discord_admin_users is a list' explicitly and treat anything else as 'no admins' (fail closed, as for invalid JSON), or add AttributeError/TypeError to the except lists at :173 and :82 in line with :266.

findings.trigger: In _save_admin_data_unlocked() (reached from save_admin_data and add_admin_user), load_config() at :330 runs BEFORE admins_file is assigned at :336. If load_config() raises an IOError/OSError (config directory unreadable, disk trouble), the handler at :379-381 formats f'... saving admin data to {admins_file} ...' with a name that has not been bound yet -> UnboundLocalError from inside the except block. This is not caught by any of the three handlers, so the caller gets a confusing NameError-type exception instead of the documented False, and the real cause is not logged. Same defect class the auto-action service already fixed for temp_path (review B29, :686-690).
findings.suggestion: Resolve admins_file = _admins_file() before the try (or before load_config()), or log without the path in the handler.

findings.trigger: validate_discord_snowflake('') returns (True, '') because 'empty is allowed (optional field)'. In validate_rule_data the 'at least one channel ID' test (:265) only checks that the LIST is non-empty and then validates each element with this function. A message rule with channel_ids [''] (an empty input row left in the panel) or ['', ''] therefore passes validation, is saved with success=True, and can never match any channel - the operator sees a saved, enabled rule and believes it works. The same empty-is-fine short cut is right for the optional notification_channel_id, but wrong for list elements.
findings.suggestion: In validate_rule_data, filter empty/whitespace channel_ids before the emptiness test (channel_ids = [c for c in channel_ids if str(c).strip()]) or reject empty elements explicitly; keep the optional-empty behaviour only for the single optional fields.
findings.unsure_why: Whether the panel or API can actually submit an empty string inside channel_ids is outside this section; the validator accepting it is certain.

findings.trigger: validate_rule_data normalises the action type with .upper() before checking it (:318), but ActionConfig.from_dict stores data.get('type', 'NOTIFY') as given. A rule submitted with action type 'restart' or 'Restart' (an API call, a hand-edited file re-saved through update_rule) passes validation as RESTART and is written to disk as 'restart'. Inside this file already, gated_verb(action.get('type','')) at :350/:360 receives the raw value while the NOTIFY/image-update checks (:325-330) use the upper-cased one. Whether the executor compares case-sensitively I cannot see; if it does, the rule validates, saves, shows as valid and never acts (or acts as the default NOTIFY).
findings.suggestion: Normalise once and store the normalised value: set rule_data['action']['type'] = action_type (upper) in validate_rule_data or in ActionConfig.from_dict.
findings.unsure_why: The consumer of ActionConfig.type (automation_service) is outside this section; the drift between validation and storage is certain.

findings.trigger: VALID_ACTION_TYPES contains 'RECREATE', so validate_rule_data accepts a rule whose action is RECREATE and add_rule/update_rule store it with success. SPEC Z6 says there are exactly three container actions (start, stop, restart) and no remove. Either the executor implements RECREATE (which requires removing the container -> Z6 broken on the automation path), or it does not (-> a rule that validates, is saved, and silently never does what its name says). Either way the validator promises an action DDC must not or cannot perform. Trigger: create a rule with action type RECREATE via the panel/API -> 'created'.
findings.suggestion: Remove 'RECREATE' from VALID_ACTION_TYPES (and from the panel's choices) or, if it is a deliberate future action, reject it with an explicit 'not supported' message until it exists.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see whether automation_service executes RECREATE, refuses it, or whether the panel even offers it; the acceptance by the validator is certain.

findings.trigger: AutoActionRule.from_dict uses id=data.get('id', str(uuid.uuid4())) - a rule on disk WITHOUT an 'id' (hand-written, or copied from an example) receives a NEW random id on every read. get_rules() shows it each time under a different id, get_rule(id) never finds it, update_rule/delete_rule match on the raw dict's r.get('id') and answer 'Rule not found', increment_trigger_count warns 'not found' after every firing. The operator sees a rule they can neither edit nor delete from the panel and whose trigger count never moves, while it does fire. Nothing ever writes the generated id back.
findings.suggestion: Treat a missing id as invalid when reading (skip with a clear error), or assign and persist an id once (e.g. a one-time migration in _load_config_file / _ensure_config_exists) instead of generating a fresh one per read.

findings.trigger: _under_lock takes cross_process_lock(self.config_file) and the protected body ends in _save_config_file(), which os.rename()s a temp file over self.config_file, i.e. replaces the inode. If cross_process_lock flocks the config file ITSELF (opens the path and locks that descriptor), then: thread A holds the lock on inode 1, renames inode 2 into place, and is still inside the block; thread B now opens the path, gets inode 2, flocks it successfully (nobody holds inode 2) and reads/writes concurrently - exactly the read-modify-write race the decorator exists to prevent (the docstring's 'panel answered created for a rule that was not on disk'). The same pattern is in admin_service (cross_process_lock(_admins_file()) around os.replace of the same path, :293/:310 with :364). If cross_process_lock uses a separate sidecar lock file, there is no problem.
findings.suggestion: Make sure cross_process_lock locks a sidecar file (e.g. <path>.lock) that is never renamed over, not the data file; if it already does, a one-line comment at the decorator saying so would stop the next reader from having to check.
findings.unsure_why: utils/atomic_io.cross_process_lock is outside this section; I cannot see which file it locks.

findings.trigger: add_rule (and update_rule at :803) validates the rule name on the RAW value (:245-248: non-empty, <= 100 chars) and only afterwards sanitizes it with sanitize_string, which strips '<' and '>' and then .strip()s. A name consisting only of those characters, e.g. '<>' or '<<< >>>', passes 'Rule name is required' and is saved with name '' - success=True, and the panel then shows a rule with no name at all. Validation and sanitization look at two different strings.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize first and validate the sanitized name (or re-check the sanitized name for emptiness before saving).

findings.trigger: The comment promises 'DDC never publishes its translations, so this opens no loop', but the loop protection for crossposted messages does not depend on DDC alone. State: a DDC target channel is an announcement channel in which a third party publishes messages (a human pressing Publish, or one of the common auto-publish bots), and a DDC source channel - directly or through another server - follows that channel. Discord then delivers DDC's own translation back as a webhook post with IS_CROSSPOST set; :47 lets it through because of the exception, :55 does not catch it because the crossposted copy has a new message id, and it is translated again -> published again -> ... The 2026-09-26 loop was closed for bots/webhooks; the 2026-09-27 exception reopens exactly one door and the comment overstates why it is safe.
findings.suggestion: Either accept and document the residual risk ('if a target channel is published and followed back into a source channel, a loop is possible'), or let the service recognise its own content on the way back (e.g. compare the crossposted message's content/author name with recently posted translations, or keep a set of the translation texts it sent).
findings.unsure_why: It needs a configuration where a published target channel is followed by a source channel, which may be considered an operator error; and whether the TranslationService rejects the message on another criterion I cannot see.

findings.trigger: get_rules() wraps AutoActionRule.from_dict in 'except Exception: logger.error("Skipping invalid rule data")'. A rule whose 'trigger', 'action', 'safety' or 'source_filter' is null (a hand edit, an export from another tool) raises AttributeError in from_dict (:567-571, :472-475) and is dropped from the list: the panel shows one rule fewer with no marker, automation does not run it, but update_rule/delete_rule still see it in the raw file. The operator has no way to see from the panel that a rule exists but is being ignored - only the log knows.
findings.suggestion: Surface skipped rules to the caller (e.g. return them as disabled placeholder rules with the error in metadata, or expose a count/list of unreadable rules that the panel can show) rather than dropping them silently from the result.
findings.unsure_why: Whether the panel or a health check reads the ERROR log entry and shows it to the operator is outside this section.

findings.trigger: update_global_settings validates only the two alert-webhook fields (:868-871) and then does current.update(settings) with everything else unchecked. Send protected_containers as a string ('ddc,portainer' instead of a list), or global_cooldown_seconds as '30' (string), or enabled as 'false' (a non-empty string, truthy): success=True and the values are written. Within this file the first case already misbehaves: validate_rule_data does [p.lower() for p in protected_containers] (:335), which on a string yields ['d','d','c',...] so the 'container is protected' warning never appears for a rule targeting ddc; how the runtime protection and the cooldown consume the other two I cannot see. A setting that is meant to protect DDC itself is accepted in a shape that disables it, with success reported.
findings.suggestion: Validate types and ranges of every known global setting before merging (protected_containers: list of str; global_cooldown_seconds: int within bounds; enabled: bool) and reject unknown keys or at least unknown types, the same way validate_rule_data does for rules.
findings.unsure_why: Whether the panel form parser already coerces these fields before calling the service is outside this section; the service itself accepting them is certain.

notes: Depends on code I could not see, stated here rather than as findings: (1) utils/atomic_io.cross_process_lock - which file it locks decides F10, and whether the admin writes are equally affected. (2) services/automation/alert_webhook.valid_url('') - update_global_settings passes '' when the caller omits alert_webhook_url (:868); if valid_url('') is False, every partial settings update that does not carry the webhook fails with 'The alarm webhook must be an http(s) URL'. Likewise alert_webhook_mode present as None/'' fails the MODES check. (3) validate_rule_data runs INSIDE _under_lock (via add_rule/update_rule) and calls player_gate.normalize_options/query_problems and automation_service._resolved (:347-362); the decorator docstring says nothing decorated calls anything decorated - that holds for this file, but if _resolved or query_problems ever calls a decorated method of this service, the same thread flocks the same file twice and blocks for ever. (4) TranslationMonitor.on_message forwards every non-bot guild message including system messages (pins, joins; message.type is not checked) and messages with neither content, embeds nor attachments; whether TranslationService.process_message filters those I cannot see. (5) AdminService cache invalidation at :372-374 is done without _cache_lock; a get_admin_users() running concurrently in another thread can re-store the old list with a fresh timestamp right after the clear, so a removed admin could stay cached for up to 5 minutes - a narrow race, not listed as a finding. (6) Two defaults for protected_containers drift: _ensure_config_exists writes ['ddc','portainer'] (:653), get_global_settings falls back to ['ddc'] (:743) when the key is missing - low impact, no separate finding. (7) _load_config_file raises ConfigUnreadable also for FileNotFoundError (IOError), so deleting auto_actions.json while running makes every write refuse with 'repair or restore the file first' until restart; safe side, message slightly misleading. (8) The ReDoS heuristic in validate_regex_pattern is necessarily incomplete (e.g. '(a|ab)*c', '\d+\d+' pass); whether the matcher bounds execution time I cannot see - no concrete guarantee is broken, so not a finding. (9) TranslationManager._load_translations resets _translations to {} before refilling (:38) without the lock being taken by readers, so a translate() during a hot reload can briefly return English or the raw key; cosmetic. (10) Contradiction with SPEC noted in F8: VALID_ACTION_TYPES lists RECREATE although Z6 allows exactly three actions.
